name: The Spalding household at 1709 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_spalding_jesse

present_on_scene_date.note: The household is listed at 1709 Prairie Avenue in both the 1904 and 1905 editions of the Blue Book, which bracket 1 July 1904, but not with the same people: the 1905 list prints 1709 Mrs. Jesse Spalding. Each person's own note says which of them the later list drops or adds.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 1709, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census (ED 40, T623 roll 245) was read for this card. The five live-in staff it lists at the house on 1 June 1900 are on the card, graded inferred because the count was taken four years before the scene. Left off: Jessie Spaulding (an unmarried daughter of 29 in 1900 whom the 1904 Blue Book does not list (no "& dr.")). The 1910 census was not read. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: Jesse Spalding
persons.note: The 1905 edition lists Mrs. Jesse Spalding alone at 1709; when he left the household, or died, is not on either page, so his presence on 1 July 1904 is not documented. The 1900 census lists J. Spaulding here as head, born May 1830, in United States, married, lumberman (ED 40, sheet 1A, line 20, leaf n794).

persons.name: Mrs. Jesse Spalding
persons.note: The 1900 census lists Adelia Spaulding here as wife, born May 1830, in United States, married (ED 40, sheet 1A, line 21, leaf n794).
